hypothesis: The production combined model (COMBINED_POLICY, combined-weighted-v1) can be improved by two previously unused degrees of freedom: the soft present-digit probabilities from the present-digit model, and an explicit SP/DP kind-mass tilt. All candidates are evaluated against the actual frozen production policy, not a no-adjustment baseline.

selection.step_1: Keep candidates whose development rate is at least the production development rate for the same task.
selection.step_2: Among survivors, choose the highest validation rate; ties break on lower added complexity, then higher development rate.
selection.step_3: If no candidate survives step 1, keep production unchanged for that task.
selection.note: The extension block is scored only after selection.json is written and hashed. The audit block was used to select the production policy itself and is descriptive only.

limitations: Retrospective experiment on previously inspected dates. The production policy was selected on development/validation/audit blocks by combined_prediction_v1.
The October extension was used by combined_prediction_v2 to select different candidates; it is only semi-fresh for the new candidates defined here, which were never fitted or selected on it.
Panel and DP model coefficients are frozen production code; they are not refitted here.
No production files, settings, or user-facing predictions are changed.
SP/DP rates are conditional on the actual panel type; all10/all30 rates use every event.
The soft present-digit probabilities were exported by combined_prediction_v1 and never used by any candidate in v1 or v2.
